summary: Luau assert returns its first argument when it is truthy.
Luau assert returns all arguments unchanged when its first argument is truthy.
Luau assert succeeds when its first argument is a truthy expression.
Luau assert evaluates later arguments in multi-argument calls.
Luau assert(false) raises assertion failed.
Luau assert(nil) raises assertion failed.
Luau assert() raises missing argument #1.
Assert failure errors caught by pcall include the failing chunk name and source line.
Luau assert failure uses a string message argument when provided.
Luau assert failure uses luaL_optstring: nil defaults, strings and numbers become messages, and other values raise a string-expected argument error.
Number greater-or-equal uses Luau numeric comparison semantics.
Number greater-than uses Luau numeric comparison semantics.
Number less-or-equal uses Luau numeric comparison semantics.
Number less-than uses Luau numeric comparison semantics.
If/else executes the else branch when the condition is nil or false.
If/else executes the then branch when the condition is truthy, including 0.
If/elseif chains evaluate later conditions when earlier conditions are false and execute the first truthy branch.
If/elseif chains without an else block execute no branch when every condition is false.
If/elseif/else chains execute the else block when every condition is false.
If without else skips the then block when the condition is nil or false.
If-expressions evaluate constant true, false, and nil conditions with Luau truthiness.
If-expressions evaluate runtime condition expressions and choose the matching branch.
If-expression elseif chains evaluate later conditions only after earlier falsey conditions and choose the first truthy branch.
If-expressions can nest another if-expression in the else branch to model else-if chains.
If-expressions can appear as the condition of another if-expression.
If-expressions evaluate only the selected branch expression.
If without else executes the then block when the condition is truthy.
Continue in a numeric for loop skips the rest of the body and advances to the next iteration.
Continue in a while loop skips the rest of the body and re-evaluates the condition.
Continue in a repeat/until loop skips the rest of the body and evaluates the until condition.
Continue in a repeat/until loop preserves captured body locals used by closures in the until condition.
While loops evaluate their condition before each body iteration.
Repeat/until loops execute the body before testing the exit condition.
Break exits the nearest enclosing loop.
Repeat/until conditions can reference locals declared in the repeat body.
Do blocks create a nested statement block and support loop control statements inside enclosing loops.
Generic for loops bind iterator results and run their body until the iterator stops.
Generic for loops keep internal iterator state protected from assignments to visible loop variables.
Generic for loops bind multiple visible variables from iterator results.
Generic for loops bind visible variables without iterator results to nil each iteration.
Generic for loops can iterate a table constructor expression directly, visiting array and hash entries with raw table traversal.
Generic for loops expand an iterator expression call into iterator, state, and initial control values.
Generic for loops call iterator values through ordinary call semantics, including table and userdata __call metamethods.
Generic for loops honor runtime substitutions of global pairs, ipairs, and next instead of using builtin traversal shortcuts.
Generic for loops over table values traverse raw table entries when no __iter metamethod is present.
Generic for loops over table and userdata values call __iter to obtain iterator, state, and initial control values.
Generic for over a non-iterable value raises a runtime iteration error.
Numeric for loops evaluate start, limit, and optional step and run inclusive Luau iteration.
Numeric for loops coerce string start, limit, and step expressions to numbers before iteration.
Numeric for loops honor explicit positive and negative step values.
Numeric for loops keep the internal loop index protected from assignments to the visible loop variable.
Numeric for loops treat zero step as backward iteration per Luau 0.709/Lua 5.1 behavior.
Numeric for loops with a NaN limit iterate zero times.
Numeric for loops treat NaN step as backward iteration for the initial bounds check.
Numeric for loops exit when the internal index becomes NaN mid-iteration.
The upstream basic.luau concat helper joins tostring results with commas for derived fixtures.
Number equality uses Luau equality semantics.
Number inequality uses Luau ~= semantics.
Table equality uses object identity when no __eq metamethod applies.
Assignment to an existing local updates that local.
Parallel assignment evaluates RHS values before updating local targets.
Compound += assignment updates the target with Luau addition semantics after evaluating the RHS once.
Compound assignment to a table field reads the current value, applies the operator, and writes the result back.
Compound assignment to a table index evaluates the table/key target once and writes the operator result back.
Multiple assignment evaluates table targets before RHS values and stores after RHS evaluation.
Parallel assignment evaluates RHS values before updating mixed local, global, and table targets.
Bare names without a local binding resolve through the global environment table, and assignment writes that table.
Reading an absent global returns nil.
_G refers to the current global environment, and field/index writes are visible through equivalent global table reads.
Local declarations bind a single name from one initializer value.
Extra local initializer values beyond the binding count are evaluated then discarded.
Missing local initializer values bind nil.
Local declarations can bind multiple names from an initializer list.
Logical and returns the falsey left operand without evaluating to a boolean.
Logical and returns the right operand when the left operand is truthy.
Logical or returns the right operand when the left operand is falsey.
Logical or returns the truthy left operand without evaluating to a boolean.
Luau conformance harness installs print for banner statements in non-verbose runs.
print is a first-class global function value in the Luau base environment.
getfenv with the current stack level returns the active global environment table, so writes through it affect global name lookup.
getfenv on a native host function returns the thread global environment table.
setfenv(function, table) changes the target closure's global environment and returns the function.
setfenv(function, table) applied to the currently running function is visible through getfenv(1) and subsequent global lookup in that frame.
setfenv(native function, table) raises a catchable error instead of changing the native function environment.
setfenv(level, table) changes an active caller frame's environment, and getfenv(level) observes it.
setfenv(0, table) changes the thread environment and returns no values.
setfenv(0, table) changes the thread environment used by subsequently loaded chunks without changing the current function's environment.
Function calls are valid Luau statements.
Function calls can use a trailing string literal as the sole argument.
Function calls can use a trailing table constructor as the sole argument.
Long bracket strings lex as raw string literals.
Long bracket strings skip one newline immediately after the opener.
Long bracket strings use '=' levels so lower-level bracket pairs inside the content do not close the string.
Long bracket comments use level-matched delimiters and produce no tokens.
Bare and repeated semicolons are syntax errors, not empty statements.
Parenthesized call arguments must start on the callee's final line. String and table arguments may start on the next line.
Unary not maps false to true.
Unary not maps nil to true.
Unary not maps true to false.
Unary minus negates numeric values using Luau f64 semantics.
Number addition produces Luau f64 results.
Number division always produces Luau f64 division results.
Decimal exponent numeric literals parse to f64.
Floor division uses Luau floor-toward-negative-infinity semantics.
Hex integer numeric literals parse to f64.
Binary integer numeric literals with 0b or 0B prefix parse to f64.
Numeric source literals allow underscore digit separators that do not affect the parsed f64 value.
Leading-dot float literals parse to f64.
Percent operator uses Luau floored modulo semantics.
Modulo preserves observable negative zero where Luau does.
Number multiplication produces f64 values.
NaN-producing numeric operations produce Luau numeric NaN values that tostring renders as "nan".
Exponentiation uses Luau numeric power semantics for finite numeric results.
Sign of zero is preserved in numeric values and observable through tostring except at table-key normalization.
Arithmetic operators coerce numeric strings, including hexadecimal and hex-float numeric strings, to numbers before using metamethod/error paths.
Unary minus uses the same Luau numeric-string coercion path as binary arithmetic, including whitespace-trimmed decimal/hex/hex-float strings and rejection of lexer-only runtime strings.
Number subtraction produces Luau f64 results.
String values preserve byte values including embedded NUL bytes from decimal escapes.
String concatenation joins string operands and is right-associative.
String concatenation coerces number operands to strings.
String concatenation raises an ordinary Luau error when either operand cannot be coerced to string.
The length operator on strings returns the byte length.
String relational operators compare string byte sequences lexicographically.
Short quoted strings accept UTF-8 source text.
Decimal and hexadecimal string escapes preserve byte values above 127.
Unicode string escapes encode codepoints up to 0x10FFFF as UTF-8 bytes, including surrogate byte sequences used by utf8 invalid-input tests.
Backslash-newline in a short string inserts one normalized newline byte.
Unknown short-string escapes are lex errors.
Unescaped raw newlines in short strings are lex errors.
string.byte returns numeric byte values for one-based or negative indices, clamps explicit range starts below 1, and returns no value when the selected range is empty or out of bounds.
string.char builds a byte string from integer byte values in the inclusive range 0..255 and returns errors for out-of-range values.
string.char accepts at least 256 arguments when constructing byte strings from expanded result lists.
string.find returns the one-based start index as its first result when a match is found, can expand start/end results into assignments, and returns nil when no match is found.
string.find honors the optional start index, including zero clamping, negative positions, and past-end nil results.
string.find coerces numeric-string init arguments and truncates fractional init arguments like Luau integer arguments.
string.find performs plain byte search when the pattern has no magic characters or the fourth argument is truthy.
string.find with an empty pattern returns the normalized start position.
string.find supports dot-pattern wildcard matching for first-result search cases.
string.find treats percent-escaped non-alphanumeric pattern bytes as literal bytes in first-result search cases.
string.find supports the anchored syntax-error chunk-prefix pattern with percent-escaped brackets and a greedy dot-star span.
string.find supports the anchored uppercase-or-underscore class pattern used by upstream table global cleanup.
string.find supports the ASCII control-byte %c class in anchored whole-string patterns.
string.find supports the anchored whole-string utf8.charpattern check used by the upstream UTF-8 validator.
string.find supports byte-oriented non-capturing Luau patterns with classes, bracket classes, anchors, and repetition suffixes.
Recognized anchored string patterns return no match, not an unsupported-pattern error, when init starts after byte one.
string.match returns the matched substring for plain and simple dot-pattern first-result cases, and nil when no match is found.
string.match supports an anchored pattern with a greedy dot-star span and literal prefix/suffix.
string.match returns captured substrings for the decimal line-number capture used by upstream error stack parsing.
string.match returns one-based byte positions for empty captures.
string.match supports numeric backreferences to earlier captures.
string.match supports nested captures with greedy backtracking.
string.gsub replaces non-overlapping plain byte pattern matches and returns the replacement count.
string.gsub supports the %s+ ASCII whitespace-class repetition used by the upstream constructs line-rewrite fixture.
string.gsub supports the (%p) single-capture punctuation escaping pattern used by upstream syntax-error checks.
string.gsub supports the raw byte-class range used by upstream UTF-8 continuation-byte stripping.
string.gsub byte classes support percent classes and their complements inside bracket classes and as single pattern atoms.
string.gsub dot patterns match every byte including NUL.
string.gsub treats %1 as the whole match when the pattern has no explicit captures.
string.gsub calls function replacements with captures or the whole match and keeps the original match when the function returns nil or false.
string.gsub uses the first capture or whole match as the table replacement key and keeps the original match for nil or false replacement values.
string.gsub supports the anchored optional-capture insertions used by upstream pattern-position helpers.
string.gsub supports captured pattern items with repetitions, numbered replacement captures, and %0 whole-match replacement.
string.gsub supports one-based position captures and passes them to string and function replacements.
string.gsub empty patterns replace the start position, each byte boundary, and the end position while advancing after zero-width matches.
string.gsub supports %bxy balanced byte-pattern matches for parentheses and quoted spans.
string.gsub rejects unfinished captures, unmatched closing captures, invalid replacement capture indexes, and invalid numeric backreferences.
string.gmatch returns an iterator closure over non-overlapping plain byte-pattern matches.
string.gmatch supports the non-newline run pattern used by upstream stack traceback scanning.
string.gmatch supports the ASCII %w+ word-run pattern used by upstream pattern-match tests.
string.gmatch iterates substrings matched by utf8.charpattern.
string.gmatch returns one-based byte positions for the empty-position capture before utf8.charpattern.
utf8.charpattern exposes Luau's byte-pattern constant for one UTF-8 codepoint.
utf8.char encodes zero or more Unicode codepoints into Luau byte strings.
utf8.codepoint decodes codepoints from a one-based byte range and rejects invalid UTF-8 byte sequences.
utf8.codes returns an iterator triple that yields one-based byte positions and decoded codepoints.
utf8.len counts valid UTF-8 characters in a byte range and returns nil plus the invalid byte position for malformed input.
utf8.offset returns one-based byte positions for relative UTF-8 character offsets and rejects continuation-byte starts.
utf8 library error paths use Luau-compatible substrings for invalid codepoints, invalid byte sequences, and out-of-range positions.
utf8 library functions ignore unused extra arguments where Luau 0.709 only reads the documented parameters.
buffer.create returns a buffer value with the requested byte length.
vector.create returns a vector value from numeric components.
string.format %s substitutes string or number arguments as strings.
string.format integer directives format signed decimal, unsigned decimal, octal, and hexadecimal integer views.
string.format %c emits byte characters including NUL and high-byte values with width and left-alignment handling.
string.format floating-point directives format fixed and exponent forms with Luau/C-style default precision and exponent padding.
string.format %q quotes strings with Luau escapes for quotes, backslashes, newlines, carriage returns, and NUL bytes.
string.format applies Luau width, zero-padding, left-alignment, and precision controls for the implemented string/integer directives.
string.format %% emits a literal percent sign without consuming an argument.
string.len returns the byte length of strings and coerces numeric inputs to strings.
string.lower maps ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase and preserves other bytes.
string.pack encodes integer, float, padding, alignment, fixed-string, zero-terminated, and sized-string format options into exact byte strings using Luau's format sizes.
string.packsize computes fixed-format byte sizes with Luau alignment rules and rejects variable-length formats.
string.unpack decodes packed byte strings into values and returns the next one-based byte position.
string.pack, string.unpack, and string.packsize raise script-observable errors for invalid sizes, alignment, overflow, short data, and zero-containing z strings.
string.rep repeats a string count times, returns empty for non-positive counts or empty input, and ignores separator-style extra arguments.
string.reverse reverses string bytes and preserves embedded NUL/control bytes.
string.split with an empty separator returns one array entry for each byte in the input string.
string.split splits on a literal separator, preserves trailing empty fields, and returns the whole input when the separator is absent.
string.sub returns a byte-indexed substring with Luau one-based, negative-index, and clamped range semantics.
String method calls index the string library table and pass the string as the implicit self argument.
string.upper maps ASCII lowercase letters to uppercase and preserves other bytes.
bit32.band, bit32.bor, bit32.bxor, bit32.btest, and bit32.bnot operate on arguments reduced to uint32 and return exact 32-bit numeric results.
bit32.lshift, bit32.rshift, and bit32.arshift implement Luau logical and arithmetic 32-bit shifts, including negative displacements and shifts at or beyond 32 bits.
bit32.lrotate and bit32.rrotate rotate uint32 values by displacement modulo 32.
bit32.extract and bit32.replace read and write uint32 bit fields with Luau bounds errors.
bit32.countlz, bit32.countrz, and bit32.byteswap return Luau uint32 count and byte-swap results.
bit32 functions accept numeric strings through normal number coercion and reject nonnumeric or out-of-range arguments with catchable errors.
ipairs iterates array table elements with one-based numeric keys.
ipairs stops at the first nil array element.
ipairs returns the raw array iterator function, the table state, and initial control value 0 for manual iterator calls.
ipairs and its inext iterator use raw array indexing, stop at raw nil slots, and do not invoke __index or __len metamethods.
next returns nil or the next key when used in single-result contexts.
next iterates non-nil array table slots with one-based numeric keys when used directly in generic for.
next iterates hash table entries when used directly in generic for.
pairs iterates non-nil array table slots with one-based numeric keys.
pairs continues past nil array holes and visits later non-nil array slots.
pairs iterates hash table entries and returns their keys and values.
pairs over hash keys can continue when the loop body removes the current key.
pairs returns next, the table state, and nil control for manual iterator calls.
table.foreach calls a function with each key/value pair and returns the first non-nil callback result.
table.foreachi calls a function for integer keys from 1 through the legacy n length or array length and returns the first non-nil callback result.
table.concat joins array table elements with a separator, coercing numeric elements to strings.
table.concat honors start and end range arguments for array slots.
table.concat reads numeric hash keys when an explicit range selects them.
table.getn returns the array length for sequential table entries.
table.maxn returns the largest positive numeric key, including numeric hash keys and ignoring nonnumeric or negative keys.
table.create converts its size argument with Luau integer coercion, rejects negative or overflowing sizes, and returns a table with a pre-sized array part filled with nil or the optional value.

table.find probes consecutive positive integer keys from the optional start index, treats nil init as 1, stops at the first nil, and returns the first index whose value equals the needle; full upstream behavior also dispatches __eq for metatable-backed equality.
table.find compares candidate values with the needle through Luau equality, including __eq dispatch and metamethod side effects.
table.freeze shallow-freezes a mutable table, returns the same table, and raises the readonly table error when called on an already frozen table.
table.isfrozen returns whether a table is readonly.
table.clone shallow-copies array and hash entries, preserves the metatable, returns a mutable clone, and rejects protected metatables and non-table inputs.
table.insert appends at #t+1 with two arguments, shifts existing array entries for in-range explicit positions, and rawsets explicit positions outside the current array length.
table.insert with an explicit NaN position completes without a catchable error; the exact resulting key is intentionally not specified by the upstream test.
table.insert mutates the table and returns zero values when observed through select("#", ...).

table.remove defaults nil or omitted position to #t, shifts remaining array entries down for valid positions, returns the removed value, and yields nil when invalid-position no-results behavior is observed through a scalar assignment context.
table.pack returns a table with positional arguments and an n field that counts all arguments, including nil.
Global unpack aliases table.unpack and returns a variable result list with the same range and nil-hole semantics.
table.unpack returns the table values from i through j as a variable result list, defaults i to 1 and j to #t, and preserves nil holes in explicit ranges.
table.unpack returns no values when the requested end index is smaller than the start index.
table.unpack raises "too many results to unpack" when the requested result count exceeds Luau's native result-list limit.
table.clear removes all observable array and hash keys, keeps the table reusable, raises "table expected" for missing/non-table arguments, and errors on readonly tables.
table.move copies raw values from a source integer-key range into a destination integer-key range, defaults the destination table to the source table, and returns the destination table.
table.move handles same-table overlapping ranges by copying in the direction that preserves original source values.
table.move raises an error containing "table expected" when either the source or explicit destination argument is not a table.
table.move raises Luau range errors for too many elements and destination index wrap-around.
table.sort sorts the array portion in place with default less-than or an optional comparator function, and ignores extra arguments.
table.sort rejects a non-function comparator argument even when the array portion is empty.
table.sort default ordering dispatches __lt metamethods for table elements.
select("#", ...) returns the number of following arguments, counting nil values.
select(n, ...) with a positive index returns all arguments from that one-based position onward.
select(n, ...) with a negative index counts backward from the end and returns values from the adjusted position onward.
select(n, ...) accepts a numeric string selector and applies normal integer index adjustment.
select reports an index-out-of-range error for zero or too-negative indices.
pcall returns true followed by all protected function results when the call succeeds.
pcall catches an ordinary Luau error and returns false plus an error object.
pcall can yield from inside the protected function and later resume with true followed by all protected function results.
Nested pcall frames remain protected across coroutine yields and resume with each protected success flag.
pcall catches an ordinary Luau error raised after a coroutine yield/resume and returns false plus the error object.
The upstream PCall conformance helper `cxxthrow` raises "oops" and pcall catches it as false plus the message.
The upstream PCall conformance helper `resumeerror` injects a guest error into a suspended coroutine so a protected call can catch it.
In the PCall conformance harness, table.create beyond the allocation cap raises "not enough memory" as a catchable Luau error.
xpcall returns true followed by all protected function results when the call succeeds.
xpcall can yield from inside the protected function and later resume with true followed by all protected function results.
xpcall catches an ordinary Luau error raised after a coroutine yield/resume and calls the error handler.
xpcall returns "error in error handling" when a deferred error handler raises after the protected function yielded.
xpcall and nested pcall protected frames preserve success results across a coroutine yield chain.
xpcall catches an ordinary Luau error, calls the error handler with the error object, and returns false plus the handler's first result.
xpcall calls debug.traceback before unwinding the protected error stack, preserving the error message and protected call frame in the traceback.
xpcall calls debug.traceback for a protected error raised after coroutine yield/resume, preserving the deferred error message and protected call frame in the traceback.
xpcall returns "error in error handling" when the error handler itself raises an ordinary Luau error.
xpcall reports missing or non-function error-handler arguments before running the protected function.
pcall and xpcall close open upvalues while handling an immediate protected-call error, before callers or handlers can read them.
pcall closes open upvalues while handling a protected-call error raised after a coroutine yield.
coroutine.close returns false plus the stored coroutine error when closing a coroutine that died with an error.
error with a string message raises that message as the Luau error object, with source prefixing handled by the call boundary.
error with level 0 raises a string error object without any position prefix.
error with positive stack levels attributes the pcall-visible error object to the selected caller line.
error with a string message at default level prefixes the pcall-visible error object with chunk name and source line.
VM-raised runtime errors caught by pcall include the failing chunk name and source line.
VM-raised runtime errors caught by pcall report the failing line from the loaded chunk.
Unbounded guest recursion raises a catchable stack overflow error with source context instead of overflowing the host stack.
Unbounded self-tail recursion consumes logical Luau call budget and raises a catchable stack overflow error instead of looping forever.
Self-recursive non-tail call frames preserved across coroutine yield/resume continue executing parent frames after the yielded base case returns.
Self-recursive non-tail pcall frames catch ordinary Luau errors raised by an inner recursive call instead of leaking to an outer protection boundary.
Self-recursive non-tail pcall frames catch ordinary Luau errors raised after coroutine yield/resume.
Stackless self-recursive non-tail call frames remain visible to debug.traceback and debug.info as ordinary Luau stack frames.
rawequal compares values using raw Luau equality without metatable dispatch.
rawget performs a raw table read, ignores extra arguments, and does not invoke metatable dispatch.
rawset performs a raw table write, ignores extra arguments, and reports Luau table-key write errors.
rawlen returns raw table/string length and errors for other value types.
Writing to a readonly table through assignment, rawset, or mutating table-library operations raises "attempt to modify a readonly table".
tostring converts booleans to their Luau text form.
tostring errors when called with no argument, including when a sole expanded call argument returns no values.
tostring converts tables and functions to Luau-shaped identity strings with table:/function: prefixes.
tostring invokes a table or userdata __tostring metamethod and uses its string result.
tostring converts nil to the string "nil".
tostring converts numbers to their Luau text form.
setmetatable assigns a table metatable and returns the table.
getmetatable returns table and userdata metatable tables when present.
newproxy creates userdata values without a metatable by default/nil/false, and with a fresh empty metatable for true.
newproxy accepts omitted, nil, and boolean arguments only; passing userdata, table, string, number, or function values raises an argument error.
collectgarbage accepts omitted, "collect", and "count" modes in the upstream conformance harness and returns a number for these modes.
collectgarbage accepts "stop", "restart", and "step" modes with observable step completion.
gcinfo returns a numeric memory-count result.
debug.traceback includes named bytecode function frames and honors the level argument when omitting frames.
debug.info raises Luau-shaped errors for missing subject, missing options, negative levels, invalid options, and duplicate options.
debug.info reports active native and bytecode stack frame name, source, line, function, and arity metadata for supported stack levels.
debug.info reports native and bytecode function name, source, function identity, definition line, fixed parameter count, and vararg flag metadata.
coroutine.create creates a resumable thread handle and coroutine.resume returns success plus function results.
coroutine.status reports suspended before execution and dead after a completed resume.
coroutine.running returns nil in the main test context and the current thread inside a running coroutine.
coroutine.isyieldable returns true in the main yieldable Luau test context and while running a coroutine.
coroutine.create returns a thread value whose type and tostring identity are thread-shaped.
coroutine.resume rejects attempts to resume the currently running coroutine.
coroutine.wrap returns an iterator callable and coroutine.yield produces successive result lists.
string.format %* formats an argument through Luau tostring, including __tostring metamethod dispatch.
type returns Luau base type names for primitive values and tables.
type returns userdata for newproxy-created userdata values.
typeof returns the same base type names as type when no custom userdata is involved.
loadstring with a valid literal string compiles a callable chunk in Luau conformance mode.
loadstring with an invalid literal string returns nil plus an error message instead of raising an outer compile error.
loadstring with a dynamic source expression compiles a callable chunk in Luau conformance mode.
A loadstring-compiled chunk can call functions defined in the root program and nested dynamic chunks resolve those root prototypes correctly.
loadstring with invalid dynamic source returns nil plus a chunk-name-prefixed error message in Luau conformance mode.
A metatable __metatable field protects the real metatable from getmetatable exposure, setmetatable replacement, table.freeze, and table.clone.
__index and __newindex metamethods dispatch table and userdata indexing for absent keys, with function and table handlers following Luau key-validation behavior.
A table or userdata value with a __call metamethod is callable, receiving the original value as the first argument and forwarding ordinary varargs/results.
The length operator dispatches table __len metamethods, requires a numeric result, propagates metamethod errors, and rawlen ignores __len.
Numeric arithmetic operators dispatch __add, __sub, __mul, __div, __idiv, __mod, __unm, and __pow metamethods when numeric coercion fails.
The concatenation operator dispatches __concat metamethods when string/number coercion fails, passing the original operands and using the first result.
Relational comparisons dispatch compatible __lt and __le metamethods for non-primitive operands; <= and >= fall back through __lt when __le is absent.
Equality dispatches compatible __eq metamethods for table and userdata operands, including self-comparisons, while raw table-key access ignores __eq.
tonumber converts decimal numeric strings to numbers.
tonumber converts "nan" to a numeric NaN value.
tonumber without an explicit base follows Luau's strtod path for inf and infinity spellings with optional signs and surrounding whitespace.
tonumber without an explicit base follows Luau's strtod path for nan(...) payload spellings, canonicalizing the resulting NaN payload in rustia.
Runtime string-to-number conversion rejects Luau source-literal-only binary prefixes and underscore digit separators.
tonumber without an explicit base follows Luau's strtod path for hexadecimal numeric strings, including fractional mantissas and binary exponents.
tonumber with an explicit base parses trimmed integer strings in bases 2 through 36 and returns nil for invalid digits or empty strings.
tonumber with explicit base 16 follows Luau's strtoull path and accepts 0x or 0X prefixes only when followed by a hexadecimal digit.
tonumber with an explicit non-decimal base follows Luau's unsigned strtoull path, so negative signs wrap through unsigned 64-bit conversion before the f64 result is produced.
Standard library table fields expose ordinary callable function values when read and stored in locals.
math.abs returns the absolute value of numeric inputs after Luau numeric coercion.
math.abs evaluates and ignores extra arguments, raises a catchable missing-argument error with no arguments, and raises a catchable invalid-argument error for non-numeric first arguments.
math.huge evaluates to positive infinity.
math.pi evaluates to the nearest f64 representation of pi.
math.floor returns the largest integer less than or equal to the numeric input, after Luau numeric coercion.
math.ceil returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the numeric input, after Luau numeric coercion.
math.min folds one or more numeric inputs left to right using Luau numeric coercion and comparison semantics.
math.max folds one or more numeric inputs left to right using Luau numeric coercion and comparison semantics.
math.min and math.max preserve Luau's order-dependent NaN behavior by comparing each later argument against the current result.
math.sign returns 1 for positive numbers, -1 for negative numbers, and 0 for zero or NaN.
math.clamp constrains a value to an inclusive numeric range after Luau numeric coercion.
math.round rounds ties away from zero and preserves non-finite values.
math.fmod returns the C-style remainder whose sign follows the dividend after Luau numeric coercion.
math.pow raises a numeric base to a numeric exponent after Luau numeric coercion.
math.sqrt returns the square root after Luau numeric coercion.
math.deg and math.rad convert between radians and degrees using the Luau pi constant.
math.isnan reports true only for numeric NaN values after Luau numeric coercion.
math.isinf reports true only for positive or negative infinity after Luau numeric coercion.
math.isfinite reports true only for finite numbers after Luau numeric coercion.
math.sin, math.cos, and math.tan return libm-backed trigonometric results after Luau numeric coercion.
math.asin, math.acos, and single-argument math.atan return libm-backed inverse trigonometric results after Luau numeric coercion.
math.atan2 returns the two-argument arctangent after Luau numeric coercion.

Array table literals store sequential values and preserve nil holes.
The length operator returns the array length for sequential array table literals.
The length operator returns 0 for array table literals containing only nil slots.
Numeric table indexing reads one-based array slots from array table literals.
Named table literal fields assign string keys readable through dot field access.
Computed table literal keys assign the evaluated key value.
Duplicate table literal fields are assigned left to right, so later fields overwrite or remove earlier values.
Absent raw table keys read as nil when no metatable path is involved.
Non-integer numeric table keys are distinct hash keys, not array indices.
String table keys can be read through bracket indexing.
Table bracket or field assignment writes the indexed key.
Numeric keys outside positive integer array slots are stored and read as hash keys.
Raw table storage canonicalizes numeric -0 and 0 to the same table key.
Table reads using a NaN key return nil.
Table writes using nil or NaN keys raise the exact Luau table-index error.
Table raw storage and lookup use raw key identity and do not dispatch __eq metamethods.
Tables with __mode containing k remove unreachable collectable keys after collection while preserving noncollectable keys and strongly-valued self keys.
Tables with __mode containing v remove unreachable collectable values after collection while preserving noncollectable values and strongly-keyed self values.
Weak table entries are eventually cleared by automatic collection during execution without an explicit collectgarbage call.
Local function declarations bind a function value visible after the declaration.
Function calls evaluate a function value and return its first result in scalar contexts.
Anonymous function expressions create callable function values.
A local function can recursively call itself by name.
Direct self-recursive statement calls handle the upstream calls.luau depth-200 case without overflowing the host stack.
Direct self-recursive return calls handle the upstream calls.luau depth-10000 case without overflowing the host stack.
Missing fixed parameters are nil and extra call arguments are ignored in scalar fixed-arity calls.
Colon method calls evaluate the receiver and pass it as the implicit first argument.
Function declaration statements assign the created function value to the named table field target.
Colon function declarations assign the function to the named table field and add an implicit self parameter.
Method calls returning their receiver can be chained, with each colon call passing the returned table as self.
Higher-order closures can encode recursion through function values and captured parameters.
Nested closures capture parameters from enclosing functions and keep them alive after the outer function returns.
Functions can return a fixed list of multiple values.
A function call in list context expands returned values and nil-fills missing target slots.
In a local or assignment value list, only the trailing function call expands to fill remaining targets; earlier calls are scalar-adjusted.
In a return list, a trailing function call expands all returned values after the scalar prefix.
In a function-call argument list, a trailing function call expands all returned values into the enclosing call's arguments.
Nested trailing calls in a function-call argument list expand through inner and middle calls while earlier outer arguments are scalar-adjusted.
Nested functions capture and read variables from enclosing lexical scopes after closure creation.
Nested functions mutate captured variables through shared upvalue cells.
Sibling closures over the same lexical variable observe and mutate the same upvalue cell.
Closures capturing numeric for control variables receive a fresh upvalue cell for each iteration.
Closures capturing generic for control variables receive fresh upvalue cells for each iteration.
Closures capturing locals declared in a repeated loop body receive fresh upvalue cells for each declaration execution.
Tail calls from vararg functions close captured locals only after closures passed to the callee can still read them.
Functions may declare trailing varargs with ....
Vararg expressions evaluate to the current function call's extra arguments.
Trailing varargs expand into local declaration value lists with nil fill when short.
Trailing varargs expand in return lists after fixed prefix values.
Trailing varargs and calls returning varargs expand in enclosing function call argument lists.
Trailing varargs expand into array fields in table constructors.
Nested trailing calls expand their own final argument list before their results expand into an enclosing call.

Function type annotations with empty argument and return packs parse and erase at runtime.
Luau native type names, optional annotations, table shapes, and function type annotations parse and erase at runtime in the interpreter.

Explicit function and method type-instantiation suffixes parse and erase before runtime calls.
Trailing function calls expand into array fields in table constructors.

os.date("!*t") UTC date tables carry a boolean isdst field set to false.

Local type annotations parse and erase at runtime.
Type syntax has no runtime value effect.
Union type syntax parses in type context.
